A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same geometric-descriptor and geometry-guidance study. The main text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite retitling and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-generator experiments, MNIST VAE analyses, Stable Diffusion descriptor measurements and reward-guidance examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds corruption tests, quantitative reward-guidance evaluation, DiT experiments and additional manifold analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same three descriptors, 120-dimensional projected Jacobians for Stable Diffusion, and a five-bin local-scaling surrogate for gradient guidance. v2 expands the randomized-SVD and smooth-activation explanations without establishing a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds corrupted-ImageNet scenarios, face-domain OOD evaluation involving CelebAHQ/CelebA, Flickr, LFW and flowers (Fig. 16), and a nine-Gaussian toy distribution (Fig. 32). The Swiss wealth/occupation prompt comparison and chest X-ray fine-tuning task disappear. Chest X-ray evaluation data remain in the new UMAP analysis, so medical-image coverage is not wholly removed.

E2.justification: Geometry guidance remains compared with Stable Diffusion without geometry guidance, already illustrated in v1. v2 adds quantitative evaluation of that comparison but no competing guidance algorithm or OOD detector. DiT is another generator studied, not a competing method evaluated against the proposal.

E3.justification: v2 adds a quantitative guidance protocol using 2,560 generations, matched prompts/seeds, ten baseline scaling bins, four reward-training sizes and guidance selected to maximize scaling per bin. It also introduces a 0.05-distance on/off-manifold criterion and DiT-XL evaluation at zero noise. ImageNet level-set comparisons change from CFG 7.5 in v1 Fig. 9 to 3/5/7 in v2 Fig. 5. The retained MNIST plots are called MSE despite MAE axes, leaving that apparent metric change unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity tests across 16 corruptions, a reward-training-data ablation, quantitative checkpoint-dependent on/off-manifold analysis, descriptor aggregation through UMAP and a Gaussian anti-mode case study. The standalone CheXpert comparison, X-ray fine-tuning analysis and demographic/occupation comparison disappear. MNIST noise-training and descriptor-correlation analyses are largely retained and reorganized.

E5.justification: v2 Fig. 16 introduces noise-dependent t-tests between dataset scaling distributions, with a p = 0.05 reference line. Same-seed comparisons and 95% confidence intervals already appear in v1 Fig. 8 and remain in v2. No increase in repeated training runs or seed counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports quantitative guidance effects on scaling, Vendi diversity and RAHF aesthetics (Fig. 8), corruption responses (Fig. 6), and DiT diversity results (Fig. 13). Its Fig. 5 replaces v1 Fig. 9's six-panel scaling/rank comparison with scaling-only results across CFG settings; the earlier artifact-score and rank-level-set curves are absent. These are added or replaced results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The descriptor definitions and central entropy identity remain unchanged. v2 adds a change-of-variables derivation of that identity in Appendix E, approximation reasoning in Sec. 2.2, and asserted scaling/rank and neighboring-region rank bounds in Appendix C. These extend mathematical support within the existing framework.

C1.justification: The central claims connecting geometry with generation characteristics and on/off-manifold behavior persist. v2 strengthens the headline guidance contribution from controlling likelihood or uncertainty to improving both aesthetics and diversity, and explicitly claims the first large-scale analysis of foundational text-to-image manifold geometry.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies application to smooth, non-CPWL networks as first-order approximation, proposes averaging and high-frequency explanations for corruption effects, and develops interpretations of descriptor interrelationships. It also reframes classifier-free-guidance effects around conditional alignment. The original limitations concerning training dynamics and Jacobian cost remain.

D1.justification: v2 explains projection construction, identifies the RAHF preference predictor and gives separate descriptor timings on TPUv3 in Appendix A. Conversely, v1's 512-by-512 slice grid, four-dimensional neighborhood with radius 0.00001, and ten sampled noise timesteps per reward-training image are no longer specified. These disclosure changes do not establish altered implementations.

R1.justification: The new Appendix B substantially expands positioning around contractive autoencoders, VAE curvature, diffusion intrinsic dimensionality, likelihood-based OOD detection and denoiser uncertainty. It compares assumptions and claimed advantages with prior approaches and adds works such as Kamkari et al. (2024). Some new related-work citations remain unresolved question marks.

P1.justification: The introduction and contributions are extensively rewritten, the toy example is integrated into the descriptor exposition, and descriptor order changes. Former Sec. 3.3 material is reorganized into characterization and downstream-results sections, while MNIST training dynamics move to a themed appendix. The title, author list and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the toy-model and ImageNet result displays, combines positive/negative guidance panels, and adds corruption, ablation, DiT, OOD and anti-mode figures. Numerous retained ImageNet, MNIST and latent-decoding panels are relocated, reduced or combined within the conference layout. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The main gain is quantitative, matched-prompt/seed evaluation of geometry guidance (Sec. 5, Fig. 8), which v1 supported mainly through images. Controlled corruption tests and explicit non-CPWL approximation caveats also strengthen the evidence and interpretation. However, omitted implementation settings, inconsistent metric/figure references, and Fig. 31's claim of non-overlapping clusters despite visible overlap limit the net improvement.
